prompt:
I need the front end for Linecall Storm Room. Restoration messaging software for a rural electric cooperative, shown on the wall of its storm operations room during major outages, where dispatchers, line crews in the field and the member call center exchange messages about each outage.

Who's using it: Renee Okafor, the cooperative's storm desk coordinator, a former lineworker who now runs dispatch during major events. Around her in the operations room are two dispatchers, the operations manager and a member-services lead, all looking at the same messages; crews send in from trucks on their phones.

What they're doing right now: It is 2:40 a.m., nine hours into an ice storm. About 3,200 members are without power across 23 active outages. A crew just messaged that a broken pole on County Road 9 will take until mid-morning, which breaks the 6 a.m. estimate the call center has been giving 410 members on that feeder. Renee has to confirm the new estimate with the crew foreman, tell the member-services lead so the call center script and outbound text to those members can change, and answer two unread crew questions: one asking whether a mutual-aid crew from a neighboring co-op is coming, one asking where to stage for the night. Everyone in the room needs to see which messages are still waiting on a reply and who owes it.

What's in the system at this point: 11 crews (7 in-house, 4 mutual-aid from Prairie Line Electric), each with a foreman, truck number, current outage assignment and last check-in time (one crew silent for 74 minutes). 23 outage cases with an ID (e.g. OUT-1147), feeder and substation, members affected (from 3 to 410), cause (tree on line, broken pole, ice-loaded conductor, unknown), status (reported, crew assigned, en route, working, restored) and estimated restoration time with who last set it. About 180 messages since 17:30 grouped by outage, between dispatch, named crews, the call center and the operations manager; 6 awaiting a reply. Outbound member notices: 4 already sent with their text and send times, 1 draft ready. Members waiting on medical-priority callbacks: 3.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
